models_evaluated: commercially available AI triage algorithm for incidental pulmonary embolism detection

links.outcome: Report turnaround time and sensitivity with vs without AI triage notification
links.effect: Sensitivity rose from 80.0% without AI to 96.2% with AI (p = .03), specificity unchanged at 99.9%. Mean turnaround for IPE-positive exams did not differ significantly: 78.3 vs 74.6 minutes (p = .26).
links.quote: The mean report turnaround time for IPE-positive examinations was not significantly different between radiologists without AI and radiologists with AI (78.3 vs 74.6 minutes, p = .26).

openai.sample_unit: contrast-enhanced CT examinations of the chest or abdomen
models_evaluated: Commercially available AI triage algorithm for incidental pulmonary embolism detection (name not reported)

links.outcome: Radiologist IPE detection sensitivity, specificity, and report turnaround time
links.effect: Without versus with AI notifications: sensitivity 80.0% vs 96.2% (p = .03); specificity 99.9% vs 99.9% (p = .58); mean IPE-positive report turnaround 78.3 vs 74.6 minutes (p = .26).
links.quote: An AI triage system improved radiologists' sensitivity for IPE detection on CECT examinations of the chest or abdomen without significant change in report turnaround times.

links.effect: Sensitivity was 80.0% without AI vs 96.2% with AI (p=.03), with no significant difference in specificity.
links.quote: Radiologists without AI, in comparison to radiologists with AI, showed significantly lower sensitivity (80.0% vs 96.2%, respectively; p = .03), without a significant difference in specificity (99.9% vs 99.9%, p = .58), for the detection of IPE.
